input: Compare broadband providers for a better deal

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the user wants to compare broadband-only or bundled packages (TV, phone, mobile) completely changes which providers and deals are relevant.
Broadband availability varies significantly by location; some providers only serve certain areas, so the user's address or region determines which options are even viable.
Whether the user is in or near the end of a contract affects urgency and whether early exit fees are a factor in the comparison.
Having a target monthly price filters out premium plans and focuses the comparison on realistic options.
Required download/upload speed is a core technical filter — gigabit full-fibre is very different from a basic ADSL package, and the right choice depends on household usage.
The number of people and devices in the household, and what they do online (streaming, gaming, working from home), directly determines what speed tier and reliability level is actually needed.

Understanding what 'better deal' means to the user — lower price, faster speeds, better reliability, improved customer service, or a shorter contract — defines what a winning option actually looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Compare broadband providers for a better deal
gold.taskDescription: Research and compare broadband providers to find a better deal than the user's current one.

questions.title: Do you want broadband-only or a bundle with TV or phone?
questions.description: Determine whether the comparison should cover standalone broadband deals or bundled packages including TV channels and/or a landline phone.

questions.title: Which country or region are you based in?
questions.description: Identify the user's location to establish which broadband providers actually serve their area, since availability varies widely.

questions.title: Are you currently in a contract, and when does it end?
questions.description: Establish the user's contract status to factor in early exit fees and how urgently they need to act.

questions.title: What is your target monthly budget for broadband?
questions.description: Set a price ceiling to filter out plans that are out of range and focus the comparison on affordable options.

questions.title: What minimum download speed do you need?
questions.description: Determine the required speed tier — basic, superfast, or full-fibre gigabit — to narrow down suitable packages.

questions.title: How many people and devices regularly use the connection?
questions.description: Understand household demand — number of users, streaming habits, remote work, or gaming — to assess what performance level is genuinely needed.

questions.title: What would make a new deal feel like a clear win for you?
questions.description: Clarify the user's primary success criterion — whether that is lower cost, faster speeds, better reliability, shorter contract length, or improved customer service.
